q: Meta says our ROAS is great but finance doesn't see it. What's going on?
answer:
Short answer: finance’s ROAS (Net ROAS, by order date) is about 0.79x for 2026-10-22 → 2026-10-28 (vs 0.80x in the prior 7 days), so finance does not see the “great” ROAS Meta reports because the two metrics use different definitions and bases — platform-reported ROAS is placement/attribution-based and uses gross sales, while finance’s Net ROAS = contribution before ads ÷ ad spend (order-date, after COGS, fulfilment and returns).

What’s behind that (largest points first)
- Different basis: Meta’s ROAS typically uses attributed gross sales on the ad placement/reporting axis; finance’s Net ROAS here is by order date and uses contribution before ads (net of COGS/fulfilment). They are measuring different numerators and different timing, so they won’t match.
- In our recent week (2026-10-22 → 2026-10-28) finance figures: contribution margin INR 2,48,575 (up from INR 2,29,911) and ad spend INR 3,13,701 (up from INR 2,86,712). Net ROAS moved 0.80 → 0.79 (≈ -1.1% vs its usual level).
- Ad delivery/efficiency changed: impressions, clicks and landing page views fell (impressions 10,20,891 → 7,26,992; clicks 25,392 → 14,517), while CPC/CPL rose sharply (CPC INR 11.3 → INR 21.6, +91.4%; cost per landing page view INR 18.3 → INR 27.7, +51.9%). Higher cost per attention plus mix shifts explain why finance’s contribution-per‑rupee appears weaker than platform gross-sales ROAS suggests.
- Mix / Simpson effect: activity shifted between ad statuses and formats (ACTIVE/SHOP_NOW segments changed share), so an aggregate platform ROAS can look healthy while finance’s Net ROAS (which weights by contribution after costs) does not.

Worth checking:
- Compare Meta’s platform ROAS (placement/gross sales basis) next to finance Net ROAS side‑by‑side by campaign and by the same date axis to see how attribution and gross→net adjustments create the gap.

Period: 2026-10-22..2026-10-28 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-29
